transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well, I came in because my sleep has really become an issue. I’m usually a very disciplined sleeper, but... since my cousin died, I just lie awake replaying that night. And then, when I finally do drop off, I wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning from these scraps of hospital images. It's frustrating because I have to go into my board meetings feeling like I’ve only slept in pieces.
I am so sorry for your loss. How long ago did your cousin pass away?
Thank you. It's been about three weeks. There was a highway collision... and, well, this whole sleep issue has been going on ever since that night.
Outside of trying to sleep, do unwanted thoughts or images of what happened repeatedly pop into your mind during the day?

Yes, they do. It happens at odd moments, really. Especially if I hear a phone ring late, or... if I see the glare of headlights on the highway. A very sharp picture of the hospital corridor will just push into my mind, or I'll hear the police officer’s voice again. It catches me off guard, so I usually just have to pause and steady myself for a second before I can get back to my day.
Have you found yourself going out of your way to avoid driving, highways, or anything else that reminds you of the crash?

No, not really. I mean, I still have to drive to work and get to my meetings, so I haven't stopped doing that. I might feel a little tense if I'm on the highway at night, but I don't go out of my way to avoid it or anything else. I just push through it.
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually jumpy, easily startled, or constantly on guard since the crash?

Yes, I suppose I am more on guard, particularly in the car. When I drive now, I find myself constantly checking the mirrors... watching the speed of the trucks around me, and looking for where I could pull off if I had to. Even on familiar roads heading to the office, my body just stays tight. It's like I'm waiting for something to happen.
Do you find yourself actively trying to push away or avoid thoughts, memories, or feelings connected to what happened?

No, I don't think I do that. When the thoughts come, I just deal with them and wait for them to pass. I'm not trying to block them out or anything. They're unpleasant, obviously, but I don't spend my day actively trying not to think about it. I just try to keep focused on my work.
Since the loss, have you felt emotionally numb or distant and cut off from the people close to you?

Yes, I suppose I have. I mean, during the prayer gatherings, and even when my nieces tried to comfort me recently... I found myself behaving properly, doing what I was supposed to do. But I didn't feel any warmth or relief inside. It's almost as if the affectionate part of me has just gone quiet.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed intrusive distressing memories, initial and terminal insomnia, hypervigilance, and emotional blunting 3 weeks following the sudden death of their cousin in a motor vehicle accident. Although trauma-related symptoms are present, the patient consistently denies both behavioral and cognitive avoidance of trauma reminders, precluding a diagnosis of Post-traumatic stress disorder (F43.1). Furthermore, the 3-week persistence exceeds the expected time frame for Acute stress reaction (F43.0). The clinical picture best fits Adjustment disorder (F43.2).
